title: Pasar A Uses The Same Bridge
voice_notes: Warm, patient teacher. One voice. Brian v3. English prompts use language_code en; Spanish reveals use language_code es. Avoid Language Transfer branding.

segments.say: Now use the same movement rule with a new verb.
Pasar means to pass, or to pass by.
Passing by is movement. So before the next action, use pasar a.
Visit is visitar. Te means you. So visitarte means to visit you.
Say: to pass by to visit you.
segments.word: to pass by to visit you

segments.say: Voy a means I am going to. That is movement too.
segments.show:
voy a =
I am going to

segments.say: Say: I am going to pass by to visit you.
segments.word: I am going to pass by to visit you

segments.say: Hear the two bridges: voy a, then pasar a.
One stretch. Show you something is mostrarte algo.
Say: I want to pass by to show you something.
segments.word: I want to pass by to show you something

segments.say: Good. Pasar is movement, so it gets the bridge.

caption: Pasar means to pass by. Because it has movement, use a before the next action: pasar a visitarte.
